THE BRIEF

A guest room, a busy lobby and a poolside terrace need different work plans. We separate the defect, the affected area and the conditions for returning it to use. Your manager receives a defined work list, agreed access arrangements and a record by room or shared area.

✺

PROPERTY IN USE

From guest rooms to shared spaces

  • Guest rooms

    We scope door and hardware faults, damaged wall or ceiling finishes, sealant joints and fixed joinery. Water stains are recorded separately from the source investigation and subsequent finish repairs.

  • Arrival and circulation

    Reception, corridors, amenities and shared doors are assessed with guest routes in mind. We identify surfaces to protect, access to retain and any temporary work boundaries.

  • Outdoor and building systems

    We connect agreed roof, drainage, lighting and air-conditioning work with the spaces affected below. Gardens, terraces and pool-surround paving are scoped by area and material.

PROPERTY IN USE

Build the plan around actual access

  1. 01

    Confirm the room release

    We agree who provides keys, which adjacent spaces remain occupied and when power, water or air conditioning may be interrupted.

  2. 02

    Protect and complete the work

    Furniture protection, dust control, noisy tasks and waste movement are included in the work plan. Related tasks are sequenced before final finishes.

  3. 03

    Check before room return

    We record functional checks, cleaning and any drying, curing or follow-up condition that still affects use.

PROPERTY IN USE

Match the part. Respect the finish.

Door hardware models, laminate finishes, paint colours and existing equipment details help define what can be retained and what needs replacement. We identify matching limitations before agreeing the finish scope.

A maintenance visit and a room refurbishment have different material and access needs. We itemise replacement parts, investigation and additional attendances where they form separate work.

PROPERTY IN USE

Send a room-based brief

  • Location and symptoms

    Room or area number, a short fault history and photographs of the item and its surroundings help us group the work.

  • Operating window

    Tell us which rooms can be released, who controls access and the date the area needs to return to use.

PROPERTY IN USE

A clear record for the next shift

We identify completed items by room or area, note any parts still required and set out the agreed next attendance. The handover distinguishes completed work from areas awaiting a material requirement or further investigation.

We hand rooms and public areas back by agreed stage, recording what was checked, any cleaning or drying outstanding and who confirms release to guests.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can all work fit between check-out and check-in?+

We assess the task and materials before agreeing that window. Hardware adjustments may have different requirements from coatings, sealants or work that interrupts shared services. We set out the room-release conditions before booking attendance.

Can several rooms be handled under one scope?+

Yes. We group the agreed defects by room, identify repeated parts and arrange batches with your manager. Different faults remain visible as separate items so completion can be tracked room by room.
